solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Made to keep one listening and prepared for battle?

blocks.note: Made in the sense of shaped or created.
The ear is the organ that listens.

explanation.surface: Someone is kept attentive and battle-ready, as if drilled for war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One listening' is a person in the surface but an organ in the wordplay; the proverb 'forewarned is forearmed' lies behind the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To be forearmed is to be armed in advance, ready for a fight.

clue.text: Went hungry? Needing inner energy, did the opposite

blocks.note: To fast is to go without food.
E is the physics symbol for energy.

explanation.surface: Someone who went hungry needed energy and so did the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: The question 'Went hungry?' is both the source of FASTED and the thing the definition points back to: the opposite of fasting is feasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Feasting is the opposite of going hungry, which is what the clue opened with.

clue.text: Hesitation about eating one egg or several of them?

indicators.note: Turned about, the letters run the other way.

blocks.note: ER is the sound of hesitation.
O is egg-shaped, so one egg is a single O.

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates before eating an egg, or perhaps several.
explanation.walkthrough: Hesitation here is the filler sound ER; the egg is the letter O, whose shape it shares.
explanation.definitionFit: Roe is a mass of fish eggs, several of the egg just mentioned.

clue.text: One disloyal in a job, source of trouble

blocks.note: Taken as printed.
A post is a position or job.
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin.

explanation.surface: A disloyal employee is the cause of problems at work.
explanation.walkthrough: ATE is not the verb: Ate is the Greek goddess who led people into rash, ruinous acts, hence a source of trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostate abandons a faith or cause, the very picture of disloyalty.

clue.text: Suitable honour for rising figure

indicators.note: In a down answer, rising means reading from bottom to top.

blocks.note: Fit means suitable.
The OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour.

explanation.surface: A fitting award is being chosen for someone on the way up.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'rising figure' looks like an up-and-coming person; 'figure' is really the definition, a design motif.
explanation.definitionFit: In art and music a figure is a recurring pattern, which is exactly what a motif is.

clue.text: Killer of hunted animal guarding southern city once

indicators.note: The deer guards what it surrounds.

blocks.note: Deer are hunted game.
S is the abbreviation for southern.
Troy is the ancient city of the Iliad.

explanation.surface: A beast that was being hunted is killing things to protect a southern town of old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Southern city once' is not one unit: 'southern' is just S, and 'city once' is ancient Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: whatever destroys life is a killer.

clue.text: Positioned like a king in charge of subject

blocks.note: A king sits at the top of the pile.
IC is the abbreviation for in charge.

explanation.surface: A monarch sits in command of one of his subjects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject' reads as a king's subject in the surface, but it is the definition: a subject of conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the subject of a talk is its topic.

clue.text: Routine held up: nail the robber responsible for it?

indicators.note: In a down answer, held up means lifted to read from the bottom.

blocks.note: A rut is a dull routine.
A pin is a small nail.

explanation.surface: A robbery was a routine job, and someone wants to nail the thief.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick Turpin was an 18th-century English highwayman who held up coaches, so 'held up' does double duty: reversal signal and his crime.
explanation.definitionFit: By example: Dick Turpin robbed coaches by holding them up, so he is the robber behind a hold-up.

clue.text: Pal I recruit to arrange something on a wall

blocks.note: Taken letter for letter.

explanation.surface: Someone enlists a friend to help hang things on a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's own helper, the recruited pal, supplies every letter of the rail.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture rail is a moulding fixed along a wall to hang pictures from.

clue.text: Above river, study game

indicators.note: In a down answer, the piece that is above comes first.

blocks.note: To con is to study closely.
The Test is a river in Hampshire.

explanation.surface: Someone above the river studies a game.
explanation.walkthrough: The Test in Hampshire is a favourite crossword river, famous for trout fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a match or game is a contest.

clue.text: Herb adding price to alcoholic drink

blocks.note: Ale is beer.
Cost means price.

explanation.surface: A bar puts a surcharge on a herb-flavoured drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Alecost is also called costmary; the name comes from its old use in brewing ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Alecost, or costmary, is an aromatic herb once used to flavour ale.

clue.text: Warrior in hospital receiving special care

blocks.note: A san is a sanatorium.
Taken as printed.

explanation.surface: A wounded fighter is in hospital getting special treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Special care' reads as one medical phrase, but 'special' works on 'care' alone; a san is short for sanatorium.
explanation.definitionFit: Saracens were the Muslim warriors of the Crusades.

clue.text: Month in which a fast woman tempted to enter races

blocks.note: The TT is the Tourist Trophy motorbike races on the Isle of Man.
Eve was tempted by the serpent.

explanation.surface: A racy woman is lured into motor racing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A fast woman' looks like one phrase, but 'fast' belongs to the definition: the Tenth of Tevet is a Jewish fast day.
explanation.definitionFit: Tevet is a month of the Jewish calendar that contains a fast day.

clue.text: Tea and vinegar’s out for us: also meat

definitions.text: Tea and vinegar’s out for us: also meat

indicators.note: Out means disordered, so the letters are rearranged.

blocks.note: Taken as printed.
Taken as printed, with the S of the possessive.

explanation.surface: A group lists what they refuse, tea and vinegar and meat too.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue is the answer speaking: meat is out for us, vegetarians.
explanation.definitionFit: Vegetarians are people for whom meat is off the menu.

clue.text: Fine vase — it has flower, something to embellish a room?

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads.
An urn is a vase.
Taken as printed.
A flower is something that flows, a river; the Ure is in Yorkshire.

explanation.surface: A fine vase with a bloom in it is just the thing to decorate a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' wants to be a bloom in the vase; it is a river, the Ure.
explanation.definitionFit: Furniture fills and fits out a room, loosely embellishing it.

clue.text: Using fingers, mine, I count

blocks.note: A dig is an excavation, a mine.
Taken as printed.
A tally is a count.

explanation.surface: Someone counts on their fingers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine' looks like a possessive; it is the noun, a dig.
explanation.definitionFit: By derivation: digits are fingers, so doing a thing digitally is doing it with the fingers.

clue.text: Escape a tricky situation? You get illumination from above

blocks.note: On the lam means escaping.
A plight is a predicament.

explanation.surface: Getting out of a fix feels like light from heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests divine help; the definition is simply light from a lamp overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamplight usually shines down from a lamp above.

clue.text: Effort of female put down

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female.
To put food down is to eat it.

explanation.surface: A woman's hard work is belittled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put down' reads as belittle; here it means putting food down the throat.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a feat is an effort that succeeds, an achievement.

clue.text: Frame given position in bottom of the box

indicators.note: The bottom of a word is its last letter.

blocks.note: The last letter of 'the'.
To spar is to box.
The lie of something is its position.

explanation.surface: A frame is put in position in the base of a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The box' looks like a container or a television; 'the' only supplies its last letter and 'box' is the verb, SPAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An espalier is a lattice frame on which fruit trees are trained flat.

clue.text: What’s explosive about sex appeal? She once told us!

blocks.note: HE stands for high explosive.
It is an old term for sex appeal.

explanation.surface: Someone asks what makes sex appeal so potent, and a woman says she told us long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: Shere Hite wrote The Hite Report on female sexuality, so she did tell us about sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Shere Hite published her findings on sexuality, telling the public what she learned.

clue.text: Mortified drone showed sign of injury

blocks.note: A drone is a low hum.
Bleeding shows a wound.

explanation.surface: A deeply embarrassed bee or idler turns out to be wounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drone' suggests a male bee or a layabout; it is the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: someone mortified has been brought low, humbled.

clue.text: Plant needing a support, post to keep it in place

blocks.note: Post is mail.
A rest is a support.

explanation.surface: A plant needs a stake and a post to hold it upright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' is a stake in the garden picture; it is mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Mare's-tail is an aquatic plant with whorled leaves.

clue.text: Tenants may have to deal with such correspondence

definitions.text: Tenants may have to deal with such

blocks.clueFragment: Tenants may have to deal with such
blocks.note: Those who let property, landlords.
Written messages sent by post.

explanation.surface: Tenants may have to handle a pile of mail.
explanation.walkthrough: A letter is one who lets property, a landlord, so tenants deal with letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters are both landlords who let and written correspondence.

clue.text: Lightheartedness is the thing sought in duty

blocks.note: A levy is a tax or duty.
'It' is the very thing wanted, as in 'that's it'.

explanation.surface: Someone argues that a cheerful attitude is what's needed at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duty' reads as an obligation at work; here it is a tax, a levy.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: from Latin levis, light, levity is lightness of spirit.

clue.text: French city spoils Parisian female, one trapped

blocks.note: To mar is to spoil.
Elle is French for she.
I is the Roman numeral one.

explanation.surface: A French city ruins a Parisian woman who is caught there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoils' reads as booty; it is the verb, MARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Marseille is a port city in southern France.

clue.text: Bore is miserable male being shunned

blocks.note: Meagre means paltry, miserable.
M is the abbreviation for male.

explanation.surface: A tedious, gloomy man is being avoided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' is a tedious person in the surface; it is a tidal bore, a wave up a river.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagre is a tidal bore, as on the River Trent.

clue.text: Distribute everything — nothing left at the end

blocks.note: All means everything.
O looks like zero.
The last letter of 'left'.

explanation.surface: Hand out everything so there is nothing left over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing left' reads as a phrase, but 'left at the end' is the unit giving T.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to allot is to share out, to distribute.

clue.text: Inclined in education to ignore one of the three essential elements?

blocks.note: Learning is education.

blocks.clueFragment: one of the three essential elements
blocks.note: The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic.

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether schooling might skip one of the basics.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic, are the traditional basics of education, so one of them is an R.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaning means inclined, as in leaning towards an opinion.

clue.text: During prayer this person’s to make a face

blocks.note: Grace is a prayer before a meal.
This person is I, so this person's is I'M, I am.

explanation.surface: Someone admits to pulling faces while grace is said.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is 'this person', so this person's is I'M, a contraction of I am.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a grimace is a twisted face, and to grimace is to pull one.

clue.text: Sailor’s muscles

blocks.note: AB is an able seaman.
Taken as printed.

explanation.walkthrough: The possessive is taken literally: AB plus the S of the apostrophe-s.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbreviation: abs is short for abdominals, the stomach muscles.

clue.text: Keep mum involved in home decorating? Charming!

blocks.note: DIY is do-it-yourself home improvement.
Sh is the call for silence.

explanation.surface: Someone is told to keep quiet about mother's DIY and answers sarcastically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like mother; 'keep mum' means stay silent. Dishy is British slang for attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishy means attractive, charming to look at.

clue.text: Heroes sit around making conjectures

indicators.note: Letters sitting around are scattered into a new order.

blocks.note: Taken letter for letter.

explanation.surface: Idle heroes lounge about speculating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sit around' reads as lounging, but 'around' signals the letters of HEROES SIT moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: someone theorising is forming conjectures.
